references.text: Moses reminds God of the promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in the same way as in this verse where he asks God to remember His servants.
The people are described as stiff-necked, which corresponds to the description of the people's hardness in this verse.
God promises to remember His covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, which connects to Moses' prayer that God should remember the fathers.
God's promise to Abraham to give his descendants the land, which is the basis for Moses' prayer that God should remember His servants.
God's promise to Isaac to confirm the oath He swore to Abraham, which is relevant to Moses' reminder of the fathers.
God's promise to Jacob regarding the land and blessing, which connects to Moses' reference to the fathers.
Moses asks God to forgive the people's wickedness and sin, using similar terms about the people's stiff-neckedness.
Moses describes the people's stubbornness and stiff-neckedness, which corresponds to the mention of the people's hardness in this verse.
Stephen calls the people stiff-necked, reflecting the description of the people's hardness in Moses' prayer.
